stem: Which area of the Next Experience UI provides a persistent global header containing the company logo, top-level navigation, the unified search bar, and user profile controls across both classic UI and Workspaces?

options.text: The Application Navigator
The Unified Navigation header
The Form header
The Service Portal banner

rationale: The Unified Navigation header is the persistent top bar in Next Experience. It surfaces the company logo, primary navigation, the global search, and user controls, and stays in place as you move between classic UI pages and Workspaces.

distractor_notes.A: The Application Navigator is the left-side filter/menu tree (favorites, history, all apps) — it's a navigation panel inside a page, not the global header.
distractor_notes.C: The form header is the band that sits on top of a single record form. It's local to the record, not global.
distractor_notes.D: The Service Portal banner only appears inside Service Portal pages, not across the Now Platform UI.

references.title: Using the Next Experience Unified Navigation

stem: In the classic UI Application Navigator, which feature lets a user quickly narrow the visible application menus and modules by typing a partial name?

options.text: The Filter Navigator
The Breadcrumb
The Reference Lookup
The Context Menu

rationale: The Filter Navigator sits at the top of the Application Navigator and matches application menus and modules as you type — the fastest way to find a module without scrolling.

distractor_notes.B: Breadcrumbs show where you are inside a list query — they don't filter the nav tree.
distractor_notes.C: Reference lookups appear on reference fields inside forms to find related records. They aren't part of the nav.
distractor_notes.D: Context menus are right-click menus on lists, forms, and fields. They don't filter the nav tree.

stem: What is the purpose of the History tab within the Application Navigator?

options.text: It lists every record the user has ever updated, grouped by table.
It shows the user's recently visited pages and records in reverse chronological order.
It shows the audit history of the current record.
It lists the modules an admin has hidden from the navigator.

rationale: History keeps a per-user list of recently visited pages and records, newest first, so the user can jump back to something they were just on.

distractor_notes.A: There's no 'everything I've ever updated' view in the Application Navigator. Audit data lives on the record itself.
distractor_notes.C: Per-record audit history appears on the record (Activity Log, Audit), not in the navigator's History tab.
distractor_notes.D: Hidden modules are governed by roles and module visibility — not by the History tab.

stem: A user wants to add the current module to their personal Favorites list in Next Experience. Which action accomplishes this?

options.text: Select the star icon next to the module name in the navigator.
Right-click the form header and choose Save as Favorite.
Type the module name into the global search and press Enter.
Open System Properties and add the module path to glide.user.favorites.

rationale: Favorites are managed by selecting the star icon next to a module or page. The starred items appear under the user's Favorites in Next Experience and persist per user.

distractor_notes.B: There's no 'Save as Favorite' option in the form header context menu. Form headers expose record-level actions, not nav favorites.
distractor_notes.C: Typing into global search runs a search across configured indexed tables — it doesn't favorite anything.
distractor_notes.D: There is no glide.user.favorites system property. Favorites are stored per user in platform tables, managed through the UI.

references.title: Managing your favorites in Next Experience

stem: Which statement best describes how tags work on records in the Now Platform?

options.text: Tags are stored on a single, system-defined column added to every table.
Tags are user-defined labels that can be applied to records across many tables and can be private, shared with a group, or visible to all users.
Tags replace categories on incidents and changes once enabled.
Tags are visible only to the user who created them and cannot be shared.

rationale: Tags are flexible labels users (or admins) define and then apply to records across many tables. A tag's visibility can be private, shared with a group, or global, giving teams a lightweight way to group and find records without changing the data model.

distractor_notes.A: Tags aren't stored as a column on each table. They live in label tables (label, label_entry) and are associated to records through references.
distractor_notes.C: Tags don't replace categories. Category fields keep their own data; tags are an additional, free-form labeling layer.
distractor_notes.D: Tags can be private, but they can also be shared with a user group or made global. Visibility is configurable.

stem: On a standard list view, what is the primary purpose of the breadcrumb shown above the list?

options.text: It shows the user's recent navigation history.
It displays and lets the user edit the active list filter conditions.
It identifies which form section the list belongs to.
It links to the record's audit log.

rationale: The breadcrumb above a list represents the active filter conditions as clickable segments. Selecting a segment removes everything to its right, which is the fastest way to widen or narrow the result set.

distractor_notes.A: Recent navigation lives under the History tab in the Application Navigator, not in the list breadcrumb.
distractor_notes.C: Form sections are tabs/groupings inside a single record form. Lists aren't owned by form sections.
distractor_notes.D: Audit history is on the record (Activity Log, Audit related lists), not in the list breadcrumb.

stem: A user needs to update the State field on five incidents at once without opening each record. Which list capability supports this?

options.text: Related List Personalization
The List Editor
Reference Qualifier
The Form Designer

rationale: The List Editor lets users update field values directly from the list view by double-clicking a cell — perfect for quick edits to a handful of records without opening each form.

distractor_notes.A: Related list personalization controls which columns appear in a related list and their order. It doesn't enable inline edits.
distractor_notes.C: Reference qualifiers restrict which records a reference field can select. They have nothing to do with editing values from a list.
distractor_notes.D: Form Designer is for laying out form sections and fields, not bulk-editing data.

stem: Which statement most accurately describes a Related List on a form?

options.text: It is a list of records from another table that share a relationship with the current record.
It is the audit trail of changes made to the current record.
It is a list of users who have read access to the current record.
It is a saved list view stored in the user's Favorites.

rationale: A Related List shows records from another table that share a relationship with the record you're on — incidents on a caller, tasks on a change, attachments on an incident, and so on. It's how the form exposes connected data without leaving the page.

distractor_notes.B: Audit information lives in the Activity Log and Audit related lists (which are themselves related lists, but the term 'Related List' is broader and isn't synonymous with audit).
distractor_notes.C: Read access is governed by ACLs. It isn't surfaced as a generic related list.
distractor_notes.D: Favorites store navigation shortcuts (modules, pages), not embedded record collections on a form.

stem: A user with no special role wants to hide a few fields they never use from their own incident form, without affecting anyone else. Which feature lets them do this?

options.text: Form Layout (admin) — modify the form definition.
Personalize Form — adjust which fields appear for this user only.
Update Set — package the change as a customization.
Business Rule — hide the fields server-side.

rationale: Personalize Form (the per-user gear/personalize control on the form) lets an end user hide or rearrange fields for themselves only. It changes their view of the form and leaves the underlying form definition alone for everyone else.

distractor_notes.A: Editing the form via Form Layout/Form Designer changes the form for every user with that view. It also requires admin (or a delegated role), which the user doesn't have.
distractor_notes.C: Update Sets are an admin/developer mechanism for moving configuration between instances, not for personal UI tweaks.
distractor_notes.D: Business Rules run server-side during database operations. They aren't the right tool for cosmetic, per-user field visibility.

stem: An administrator wants to expose a new action on the right-click context menu of every Incident list, available to all users. Which configuration object should they create or modify?

options.text: A new List Control entry on the incident table.
A new related list on the incident form.
A new System Property under glide.ui.context_menu.
A new UI Page mapped to the list view.

rationale: List Controls define the actions, buttons, and context-menu items available on a list view for a given table. To add a right-click action on every Incident list, configure the List Controls on the incident table.

distractor_notes.B: Related lists appear on a form, not on a standalone list view. They don't drive list context menus.
distractor_notes.C: There's no general 'glide.ui.context_menu' property that adds list actions. System properties tune behavior; they don't define menu items.
distractor_notes.D: UI Pages render custom pages. They aren't how you add a context-menu action to an out-of-the-box list.

stem: A user types a phrase into the global search bar in Next Experience and presses Enter. Which statement best describes what happens?

options.text: The platform searches every column of every table in the instance.
The platform searches the tables and fields that have been indexed and are configured for global search, and groups results by record type.
The platform opens a list view of the first table that matches and runs the phrase as a filter.
The platform runs a SQL LIKE query against the user's own records only.

rationale: Global search queries the tables and fields that admins have configured for search indexes, then presents results grouped by record type (Incident, Change, KB, etc.). It's scoped, performant, and respects each user's access rights.

distractor_notes.A: Searching every column of every table would be unusable. Global search is built around configured search groups, not exhaustive scans.
distractor_notes.C: Global search doesn't pick a single table and turn into a list filter — it returns results across configured tables.
distractor_notes.D: There's no per-user SQL LIKE behavior. The platform uses indexed search and ACLs to filter what each user sees.

references.title: Global search recent queries and results

stem: Which of the following is an Embedded List on a form?

options.text: A related list that has been promoted to display directly inside a form section instead of at the bottom of the form.
A read-only summary of audit history pinned to the top of the form.
A reference field that opens a popup list when clicked.
A list view stored as a favorite for one user.

rationale: An embedded list is a related list rendered inline as part of a form section, so the connected records are visible without scrolling to the very bottom of the form. It's still a related list — just embedded.

distractor_notes.B: Audit history surfaces in the Activity Log and audit-related lists. It isn't what 'embedded list' means.
distractor_notes.C: A reference field opens a lookup picker, not an inline list of related records.
distractor_notes.D: Favorites are personal navigation shortcuts. They don't render inside forms.

stem: An admin needs to add a new custom menu — "Operations" — to the global header so it appears for users across every page. Which administration feature is the right starting point?

options.text: Configure a custom menu for Unified Navigation in the Now Experience Framework administration.
Edit the user's profile to pin a personal menu to the header.
Create a new Service Portal page and link to it from the homepage.
Add a new Application module under System Definition.

rationale: Custom menus for the global header are configured through the Unified Navigation administration tooling. You define the menu, choose what it contains, and assign the audience that should see it — and then it appears in the header for those users.

distractor_notes.B: User profiles store per-user data and preferences but don't add globally visible menus to the header.
distractor_notes.C: Service Portal is a separate experience layer for self-service end users; it doesn't drive Next Experience global header menus.
distractor_notes.D: Application modules show up inside the Application Navigator's app menu tree, not as items in the global header.

references.title: Configure custom menus for Unified Navigation

stem: A new admin is briefing a stakeholder on how data is organized in the Now Platform. Which statement is the most accurate description of the relationship between tables, fields, and forms?

options.text: Forms define columns; tables and fields are views of forms.
Tables hold rows of data, fields are the columns on those tables, and forms are the UI layouts used to view or edit a single record from a table.
Tables, fields, and forms are independent objects — none of them are related at the data layer.
A form is a table with no fields, used only for display.

rationale: Tables are where records (rows) live. Fields are the columns defined on a table. Forms are the configurable UI used to view or edit one record from a table at a time. Forms render fields; they don't define them.

distractor_notes.A: Backwards. Fields are defined on the table; forms render fields. Forms don't create columns.
distractor_notes.C: They're tightly related. Forms read from and write to fields on tables.
distractor_notes.D: A form isn't a table. It's a UI layout pointing at a table and its fields.

references.title: Now Platform forms, fields, and lists

stem: Which component of the Next Experience Unified Navigation allows a user to quickly navigate to a specific module by typing its name, even with missing letters?

options.text: Global Search
Filter field
All menu
Contextual app pill

rationale: The Filter field in the Unified Navigation supports fuzzy matching — it accommodates missing letters in queries — letting users quickly jump to a module without typing the exact name.

distractor_notes.A: Global Search searches record content across tables; it does not navigate to modules by name.
distractor_notes.C: The All menu lists all available modules but does not have a fuzzy-match filter built into the navigation bar itself.
distractor_notes.D: The contextual app pill shows where you currently are and lets you favorite that page; it does not filter modules.

references.title: Using the Next Experience Unified Navigation

stem: In the Next Experience Unified Navigation, what does clicking the ServiceNow logo do?

options.text: Opens the All menu
Returns the user to the Next Experience landing page
Opens the user preferences panel
Logs the user out of the instance

rationale: The Logo in the Unified Navigation returns you to the Next Experience landing page. Administrators can replace it with a company logo, but its function remains the same.

distractor_notes.A: The All menu is a separate control in the Unified Navigation; the logo does not open it.
distractor_notes.C: User preferences are accessed through the User menu, not the logo.
distractor_notes.D: Logging out is done through the User menu, not the logo.

references.title: Using the Next Experience Unified Navigation

stem: To navigate directly to a list view for the sys_properties table using the Unified Navigation filter field, what should a user type?

options.text: sys_properties
sys_properties.list
sys_properties.do
list.sys_properties

rationale: For a list view, enter the table name in the format name.list — for example, sys_properties.list. Using the .do suffix opens a form view instead.

distractor_notes.A: Typing just the table name searches modules by name but does not guarantee a list view.
distractor_notes.C: The .do suffix opens a form (record) view, not a list view.
distractor_notes.D: list.sys_properties is not a valid format in ServiceNow navigation.

references.title: Using the Next Experience Unified Navigation

stem: A user wants the Unified Navigation All menu to reflect the most recent module additions without clearing the browser cache. What should they do?

options.text: Log out and back in to the instance
Select the refresh icon inside the All menu
Navigate to System Properties and flush the cache
Use the Filter field to search for the new module

rationale: The All menu includes a refresh icon that obtains the latest menu items without needing to manually clear the cache or log out.

distractor_notes.A: Logging out would work but is unnecessary — the refresh icon in the All menu is the correct lightweight approach.
distractor_notes.C: Flushing the system cache from System Properties is an admin operation for server-side caching, not related to Unified Navigation menu state.
distractor_notes.D: The Filter field searches existing menu items; it does not reload the menu from the server.

references.title: Using the Next Experience Unified Navigation

stem: Which role is required to add a favorite in Next Experience?

options.text: admin
itil
No role is required
personalize_list

rationale: Adding favorites in Next Experience requires no role. Any authenticated user can favorite pages, modules, and records.

distractor_notes.A: The admin role is not required for favorites; this is a basic user feature.
distractor_notes.B: The itil role grants access to ITSM modules but is not related to the favorites feature.
distractor_notes.D: personalize_list controls list column personalization, not favorites.

references.title: Managing your favorites in Next Experience

stem: A user is viewing an incident record in the classic environment and wants to add it to their Favorites. What is the correct approach?

options.text: Select the star icon in the contextual app pill in the Unified Navigation
Select the context menu icon next to the record title, then choose Create Favorite
Right-click the browser tab and bookmark the page
Navigate to System Settings and add the URL manually

rationale: From a list or record in the classic environment, select the context menu icon next to the list or record title, then select Create Favorite. Different favorites can be saved for each view of the same record.

distractor_notes.A: The star in the contextual app pill works for Next Experience pages; for classic environment records the context menu approach is used.
distractor_notes.C: Browser bookmarks are not the same as ServiceNow Favorites and do not appear in the Favorites menu.
distractor_notes.D: There is no System Settings option to manually add URLs as favorites.

references.title: Managing your favorites in Next Experience

stem: A user types an incident number into the Unified Navigation search field and sees a preview with an 'Exact Match' tag. What happens when they select that preview?

options.text: The system opens the search results page filtered to that incident number
The user is taken directly to the matching record, bypassing the search results page
The system opens a new browser tab with the record
The system prompts the user to confirm which table to search

rationale: When a record number matches exactly, the Exact Match preview lets you navigate directly to that record without going through the search results page.

distractor_notes.A: The search results page is bypassed entirely when an Exact Match is selected.
distractor_notes.C: No new tab is opened; the record opens in the current context.
distractor_notes.D: The Exact Match feature resolves to a specific record automatically with no table confirmation prompt.

stem: On the Next Experience search results page, what does selecting a source table entry in the left-side list do?

options.text: Opens a new global search scoped to only that table
Filters the results page to show matches from only that source table
Creates a saved filter for that table in the navigator
Exports the results from that table to a spreadsheet

rationale: The search results page includes a list of source tables showing matching record counts. Selecting a source table filters the results to show records from that table only.

distractor_notes.A: No new global search is triggered; you are filtering the existing results.
distractor_notes.C: Selecting a source table does not create a navigator filter.
distractor_notes.D: There is no export-to-spreadsheet action when selecting a source table on the results page.

stem: What appears when a user clicks the empty Unified Navigation search field without typing anything?

options.text: A list of all searchable tables in the instance
Recently Searched queries and Recently Viewed search result records
A prompt to install the global search plugin
The user's saved search filters

rationale: When you select the empty search field, the system displays your most recent search queries (Recently Searched) and your most recently viewed search results (Recently Viewed).

distractor_notes.A: Clicking the empty search field does not list all searchable tables.
distractor_notes.C: Global search is a base platform feature; no plugin prompt appears.
distractor_notes.D: Saved filters belong to the list/filter context, not the global search field.

stem: Which keyboard shortcut opens the keyboard shortcuts modal for the page currently being viewed in Next Experience on Windows?

options.text: Control+Shift+k
Control+/
Control+Alt+h
Control+Alt+s

rationale: Control+/ (Command+/ on macOS) opens the keyboard shortcuts modal, which shows shortcuts specific to the screen you are currently viewing, grouped by category.

distractor_notes.A: Control+Shift+k is not a documented Next Experience keyboard shortcut.
distractor_notes.C: Control+Alt+h is not the shortcut for the keyboard shortcuts modal.
distractor_notes.D: Control+Alt+s is not documented as a keyboard shortcut in Next Experience.

stem: What is the Windows keyboard shortcut to create a new record in Next Experience?

options.text: Control+n
Control+Alt+n
Shift+Alt+n
Control+Shift+n

rationale: Shift+Alt+n (Shift+Option+n on macOS) creates a new record in Next Experience.

distractor_notes.A: Control+n is a common browser shortcut for a new tab, not a ServiceNow new record shortcut.
distractor_notes.B: Control+Alt+n is not documented as the new record shortcut.
distractor_notes.D: Control+Shift+n opens an incognito window in Chrome, not a new ServiceNow record.

stem: Which keyboard shortcut saves a record in Next Experience on Windows?

options.text: Control+Enter
Control+s
Control+Shift+s
Alt+s

rationale: Control+s (Command+s on macOS) saves the current record in Next Experience.

distractor_notes.A: Control+Enter is not the documented save shortcut in Next Experience.
distractor_notes.C: Control+Shift+s is not documented as a save shortcut.
distractor_notes.D: Alt+s is not a documented Next Experience keyboard shortcut.

stem: Which Next Experience start page option is described as a deprecated feature that is read-only from the Tokyo release onward?

options.text: Responsive dashboards
Configurable workspace home
Homepages
User-selected landing page

rationale: Homepages are a deprecated feature. From the Tokyo release, homepages are read-only in Next Experience-enabled instances. Administrators should convert them to responsive dashboards.

distractor_notes.A: Responsive dashboards are the recommended replacement for deprecated homepages, not deprecated themselves.
distractor_notes.B: Configurable workspace home is a current, supported start page option.
distractor_notes.D: User-selected landing page is a supported, current option.

references.title: Configuring Next Experience start page options

stem: An administrator needs to configure a role-based landing page that routes users to different configurable workspaces depending on their role. Which start page option supports this?

options.text: User-selected landing page
Next Experience default landing page
Admin-selected landing page
Responsive dashboard

rationale: The admin-selected landing page option supports role-based logic that directs users to different configurable workspaces. The admin configures per-user or global landing pages, including role-based routing.

distractor_notes.A: User-selected landing page is set by individual users, not by admins applying role-based logic.
distractor_notes.B: The Next Experience default landing page is a fixed page, not role-configurable per workspace.
distractor_notes.D: Responsive dashboards are a valid start page but do not natively support role-based workspace routing.

stem: In the classic environment, what is the primary definition of a ServiceNow list?

options.text: A form that displays one record from a table
A set of records displayed from a table
A saved query stored in a user's profile
A dashboard widget that shows aggregated data

rationale: A list in the classic environment displays a set of records from a table. Users can search, sort, filter, and edit data in lists.

distractor_notes.A: That describes a form, not a list. A form displays one record; a list displays many.
distractor_notes.C: A saved query is a filter condition, not a list itself.
distractor_notes.D: A dashboard widget shows aggregated reporting data; that is distinct from a record list.

stem: What does each column in a classic environment list correspond to?

options.text: A related table in the database
A field on the table being displayed
A UI action defined on the table
A section defined on the associated form

rationale: Each column in a list corresponds to a field on the table. The list interface consists of a title bar, filters and breadcrumbs, columns of data, and a footer.

distractor_notes.A: Columns represent fields, not related tables. Related tables appear as related lists.
distractor_notes.C: UI actions are buttons or links, not columns.
distractor_notes.D: Form sections organize fields on a form view; they do not correspond to list columns.

stem: What is the purpose of a hierarchical list in the classic environment?

options.text: To display records sorted by a parent-child field relationship
To allow users to view related list records without navigating to a form
To restrict list access to users with the admin role
To merge multiple tables into a single view

rationale: Hierarchical lists allow users to view records from related lists directly within list view, without having to navigate to a form. Users expand or collapse sublists using the arrow icon.

distractor_notes.A: Hierarchical lists are about expanding related records in-place, not just sorting by parent-child fields.
distractor_notes.C: Hierarchical lists do not restrict access; administrators enable them per table.
distractor_notes.D: Merging multiple tables into one view describes a joined list or reporting feature, not a hierarchical list.

stem: An administrator enables detail rows on the Incident list and configures the Short Description field as the source. What is the effect on the list?

options.text: The Short Description column is hidden from the list, and its value appears as a detail row below each record
The Short Description field is bolded in the list to make it more prominent
The Short Description becomes a mandatory filter on the list
A second list view is created showing only the Short Description

rationale: When a field is designated as the source for list detail rows, the system hides the list column for that field and instead displays its value as a detail row below each record row.

distractor_notes.B: Detail rows do not bold the field; they display it below each record in a separate row.
distractor_notes.C: Detail rows have nothing to do with filters or making fields mandatory.
distractor_notes.D: Detail rows modify the existing list view in place; no second list is created.

stem: What is the definition of a form in the classic ServiceNow environment?

options.text: A list that groups records by a common field value
A view that displays information from one record in a data table
A dashboard that shows performance metrics for a single table
A template used to pre-populate multiple records at once

rationale: A form in the classic environment displays information from one record in a data table. Users can view and edit records in forms, and administrators can configure what appears on them.

distractor_notes.A: Grouping records by a field is a list feature, not a form.
distractor_notes.C: Performance metrics are shown in dashboards/reports, not forms.
distractor_notes.D: Templates can populate fields on a form, but a template is not the same as a form itself.

stem: Which form element provides access to additional functions based on record type and system setup, and can be extended by administrators using UI actions?

options.text: Related lists
Sections
Related links
Embedded lists

rationale: Related links provide access to additional functions based on record type and system setup. Administrators can add related links to forms using UI actions.

distractor_notes.A: Related lists display records in other tables with relationships to the current record, not additional functions.
distractor_notes.B: Sections group related information on the form; they are not action-based.
distractor_notes.D: Embedded lists allow editing related records without leaving the form, but are not the mechanism for additional function links.

stem: A user collapses a section on an Incident form. What happens the next time they open any record using that same form?

options.text: The section is reset to expanded by default
The section remains collapsed, as the preference is saved per user
All other users on the instance also see the section collapsed
The section is hidden permanently until an admin restores it

rationale: When a user collapses or expands a form section, the selection is saved as a user preference. The next time they access a record using the same form, the sections remain in the same state.

distractor_notes.A: The preference is persisted, not reset; the section stays collapsed.
distractor_notes.C: Form section collapse state is a per-user preference, not a global setting affecting all users.
distractor_notes.D: The section is not hidden permanently; it can be expanded again at any time.

stem: What distinguishes an embedded list from a related list on a ServiceNow form?

options.text: Embedded lists show records from unrelated tables; related lists show records from the same table
Changes to an embedded list are saved when the form is saved; related lists save immediately
Embedded lists require the admin role to view; related lists are visible to all users
Embedded lists only display read-only data; related lists allow editing

rationale: An embedded list allows editing related records without navigating away from the form, and changes are saved when the parent form is saved. Related lists save changes to their records independently.

distractor_notes.A: Both embedded lists and related lists display records from tables related to the current record.
distractor_notes.C: There is no role restriction on viewing embedded lists vs related lists.
distractor_notes.D: Embedded lists support editing; they are not read-only.

stem: In the Next Experience Unified Navigation, which area shows the user their current location in the instance and lets them favorite that page?

options.text: User menu
All menu
Contextual app pill
Notifications panel

rationale: The contextual app pill in the Unified Navigation shows where you currently are in the instance and allows you to favorite the current item if desired.

distractor_notes.A: The User menu provides access to preferences and profile settings, not current location context.
distractor_notes.B: The All menu lists all available modules; it does not show your current location.
distractor_notes.D: The Notifications panel shows alerts and notifications, not your current navigation context.

references.title: Working in the Next Experience UI

stem: Which keyboard shortcut opens the All menu in Next Experience on Windows?

options.text: Control+Shift+a
Control+Alt+a
Control+Alt+m
Shift+Alt+a

rationale: Control+Alt+a (Command+Option+a on macOS) opens the All menu in Next Experience.

distractor_notes.A: Control+Shift+a opens the Admin menu, not the All menu.
distractor_notes.C: Control+Alt+m is not a documented shortcut for the All menu.
distractor_notes.D: Shift+Alt+a is not the documented shortcut for the All menu.

stem: A user wants to add all modules under the 'Incident' application to their favorites at once. What is the most efficient method in the All menu?

options.text: Select the star icon next to each individual module one by one
Select the star icon next to the application name to favorite all its modules
Right-click the application name and choose 'Favorite all'
Navigate to System Settings and bulk-add the modules

rationale: In the All menu, selecting the star icon next to an application name favorites all the modules under that application at once, which is faster than starring each module individually.

distractor_notes.A: This would work but is inefficient when you want all modules under an application.
distractor_notes.C: There is no right-click 'Favorite all' option in the All menu.
distractor_notes.D: There is no bulk-favorite option in System Settings.

references.title: Managing your favorites in Next Experience

stem: A user creates a personal list on the Incident table that shows different columns and ordering than the default view. Who else can see this personal list?

options.text: All users who access the Incident table
Only users with the admin role
Only the user who created it
All users in the same group as the creator

rationale: Personal lists modify a specific list view according to individual preferences. They are visible only to the user who created them and do not affect other users' views.

distractor_notes.A: Personal lists are private; changing the default view for all users requires a different approach (list administration).
distractor_notes.B: Admin role does not grant visibility into other users' personal lists.
distractor_notes.D: Personal lists are not group-shared; they are strictly per-user.

stem: Which form element in the classic environment provides navigation tools and actions related to the record?

options.text: Sections
Form header
Related lists
Fields

rationale: The form header provides navigation tools and actions related to the record, such as save, insert, and navigation arrows.

distractor_notes.A: Sections group related information on the form; they do not provide navigation tools.
distractor_notes.C: Related lists display records from related tables, not navigation tools.
distractor_notes.D: Fields store specific data about the record; they are not navigation elements.

stem: A user has access to the CSM/FSM Configurable Workspace. After performing a global search, how can they view the results specifically within that workspace?

options.text: Open the workspace separately and run the search again
Select the workspace from the context menu that appears at the right of the search field after searching
Navigate to the workspace and use its built-in search bar
Filter the global search results page by source table

rationale: After performing a global search, an arrow appears at the right of the Unified Navigation search field that shows a context menu of available workspace applications. Selecting one switches the results to that workspace.

distractor_notes.A: Re-running the search is unnecessary; the context menu switch is available after the initial search.
distractor_notes.C: While workspace search is an option, the context menu within the Unified Navigation search field is the correct mechanism described in the docs.
distractor_notes.D: Filtering by source table still shows global search results, not workspace-scoped results.

stem: Which of the following best describes what Next Experience landing pages provide?

options.text: A fixed layout identical for all users showing open incidents
Role-specific information including lists, Performance Analytics data, and prioritized tasks to help users start working
A configuration interface for administrators to manage system properties
A read-only summary of the past week's activity across all tables

rationale: Next Experience landing pages provide information specific to the user's role and tasks, typically including lists, Performance Analytics and Reporting (PAR) data, and features to access new and prioritized tasks from one location.

distractor_notes.A: Landing pages are personalized by role, not a fixed incident list for all users.
distractor_notes.C: System properties are managed in System Administration, not the landing page.
distractor_notes.D: Landing pages are forward-looking (tasks to do) and role-personalized, not a read-only activity summary.

references.title: Working in the Next Experience UI

stem: Where does the Response Time Indicator appear on a ServiceNow form?

options.text: In the form header, next to the record number
At the bottom of the form
In the Related Lists section
In the breadcrumb above the form

rationale: The Response Time Indicator appears at the bottom of some forms (and lists) to indicate the processing time required to display the form.

distractor_notes.A: The form header contains navigation tools and record actions, not the response time indicator.
distractor_notes.C: Related lists display related records; the response time indicator is not placed there.
distractor_notes.D: The breadcrumb shows navigation context above the form, not performance data.

stem: In the classic environment, what is a filter in the context of a ServiceNow list?

options.text: A column header that sorts records alphabetically
A set of conditions applied to a table to display a subset of records
A saved report that aggregates data from multiple tables
A UI policy that hides fields based on record state

rationale: A filter is a set of conditions applied to a table to help you find and work with a subset of the data in that table. Breadcrumbs at the top of the list indicate the current filter conditions.

distractor_notes.A: Sorting is a separate list function; column headers control sort order, not filtering.
distractor_notes.C: Reports aggregate data; filters restrict what records appear in a list.
distractor_notes.D: UI policies control field visibility on forms, not list filtering.

stem: In a list breadcrumb showing 'Active > Category = Software > Priority = 2', what happens when a user clicks the 'Category = Software' breadcrumb?

options.text: Only the Category = Software condition is removed
All conditions to the right of Category = Software are removed, returning active software incidents
All conditions including Category = Software are removed
A new filter dialog opens to edit the Category condition

rationale: Clicking a breadcrumb removes all the conditions to its right. So clicking 'Category = Software' removes 'Priority = 2' and returns all active incidents in the software category.

distractor_notes.A: Clicking a breadcrumb removes conditions to its right, not the breadcrumb itself. To remove only one condition, click the separator (>) before it.
distractor_notes.C: Clicking 'All' would remove all conditions. Clicking a mid-breadcrumb only removes conditions to its right.
distractor_notes.D: Clicking a breadcrumb navigates/filters — it does not open an edit dialog.

stem: A developer wants to add a URL-based query that returns all active, priority-1 incidents. They right-click a breadcrumb and choose 'Copy query'. What does the copied value allow them to do?

options.text: Paste it into the global search bar to filter results
Append it to an instance URL as a sysparm_query parameter
Import it as a scheduled report definition
Use it as a UI action condition on a form

rationale: The 'Copy query' option copies the encoded query string, which can be appended to a URL as sysparm_query. For example: incident_list.do?sysparm_query=active=true^priority=1

distractor_notes.A: The global search bar accepts plain text queries, not encoded query strings.
distractor_notes.C: Encoded query strings are not imported as report definitions.
distractor_notes.D: While encoded queries can be used in reference qualifiers, the primary use described here is URL-based navigation.

stem: A user clicks 'New' while viewing a filtered list of resolved, high-priority incidents. What state does the new record open in?

options.text: A blank form with no pre-populated values
A form preset with State = Resolved and Priority = High from the active filter
A form that prompts the user to confirm the filter values before opening
A read-only preview of the filter conditions

rationale: Clicking New in a filtered list automatically applies the same filter conditions to the new record. The new form opens with the filter field values pre-populated, such as State = Resolved and Priority = High.

distractor_notes.A: The form is not blank when opened from a filtered list — filter values are applied.
distractor_notes.C: There is no confirmation prompt; the values are applied directly.
distractor_notes.D: The New button opens an editable form, not a read-only preview.

stem: By default, which users cannot see breadcrumbs or filters on a list in the classic environment?

options.text: Users with the itil role
Users with the admin role
Users with no roles
Users who are members of a group

rationale: By default, a user with no roles cannot see the breadcrumbs or filter in the classic environment. Administrators can configure the ESS portal to allow unauthenticated users to see them.

distractor_notes.A: Users with the itil role can see breadcrumbs and filters.
distractor_notes.B: Admin users have full visibility of breadcrumbs and filters.
distractor_notes.D: Group membership does not restrict breadcrumb visibility.

stem: Which roles allow a user to personalize a form in Core UI?

options.text: admin only
itil, personalize_form, or admin
No role is required
personalize_list or admin

rationale: Personalizing a form in Core UI requires the itil, personalize_form, or admin role.

distractor_notes.A: Admin is one of the required roles, but itil and personalize_form also grant this capability.
distractor_notes.C: Unlike adding favorites, form personalization does require a specific role.
distractor_notes.D: personalize_list controls list column personalization, not form field personalization.

stem: A user with the itil role personalizes an Incident form and hides the Category field. Which statement is accurate?

options.text: The Category field is hidden for all itil users on the instance
Only the personalizing user sees the Category field hidden on their view
The Category field is removed from the form definition permanently
The system prompts an admin to approve the change before it takes effect

rationale: Personal form customizations do not affect what other users see on their forms. The change is visible only to the user who personalized it.

distractor_notes.A: Form personalization is per-user, not per-role. Other itil users are unaffected.
distractor_notes.C: Personalizing does not alter the form definition; configuring the form would affect all users.
distractor_notes.D: No approval workflow is triggered for personal form changes.

stem: Which of the following actions is NOT possible through form personalization in Core UI?

options.text: Hiding a non-mandatory field from your view
Showing a field that was previously hidden by you
Adding fields that are not configured to appear on the form
Hiding a field that the form is configured to display

rationale: Form personalization does not allow users to add fields not already configured on the form. Only fields configured to display are available in the Personalize Form menu. Changing the form layout requires form configuration, not personalization.

distractor_notes.A: Hiding non-mandatory fields is allowed through personalization.
distractor_notes.B: Restoring hidden fields is allowed; clicking Reset restores the default view.
distractor_notes.D: Users can hide fields that the form is configured to display, as long as the fields are not mandatory or hidden by UI policies.

stem: What role is required to add users to a watch list on a ServiceNow record?

options.text: admin
itil
No role is required
watch_list_manager

rationale: No role is required to add users to a watch list. Any authenticated user can manage watch list subscriptions on records that have a watch list configured.

distractor_notes.A: Admin role is not required for watch list management.
distractor_notes.B: The itil role is for ITSM processes, not watch list access.
distractor_notes.D: watch_list_manager is not a ServiceNow system role.

references.title: Add users to a watch list

stem: Which watch list action allows adding someone to a watch list who does not have a user record or email address in the sys_user table?

options.text: The 'Add me' icon
The 'Add/remove multiple' icon
The 'Add email address' icon
The 'Lookup using list' icon

rationale: The 'Add email address' icon lets you enter an email address for users who are not in the User [sys_user] table or who do not have an email address defined in their user record.

distractor_notes.A: The 'Add me' icon adds the currently logged-in user — not arbitrary email addresses.
distractor_notes.B: The 'Add/remove multiple' icon opens the Edit Members window for users already in sys_user, and is only available after the record has been saved.
distractor_notes.D: The 'Lookup using list' opens the Users list to select a single user from sys_user — it requires the user to already exist in the table.

references.title: Add users to a watch list

stem: A user tries to use the 'Add/remove multiple' icon on a new, unsaved Incident record. What happens?

options.text: The Edit Members window opens normally
The option is not available until the record has been initially saved
The system auto-saves the record before opening the window
The action is restricted to admin users on new records

rationale: The 'Add/remove multiple' icon, which opens the Edit Members window, is not available until a record has been initially saved.

distractor_notes.A: The Edit Members window is unavailable on unsaved records.
distractor_notes.C: The system does not auto-save the record; the user must save it first.
distractor_notes.D: This limitation applies to all users, not specifically non-admins.

references.title: Add users to a watch list

stem: Which URL format opens a ServiceNow page with the standard banner frame and application navigator?

options.text: https://instance.service-now.com/table_name.do?
https://instance.service-now.com/nav_to.do?uri=
https://instance.service-now.com/table_name_list.do
https://instance.service-now.com/sys_id=-1

rationale: The nav_to.do?uri= format displays a page in the standard interface with the banner frame on top and the application navigator on the left.

distractor_notes.A: The .do? suffix opens a form or page directly but does not guarantee the standard framed interface.
distractor_notes.C: table_name_list.do opens a list view directly without the nav_to wrapper.
distractor_notes.D: sys_id=-1 is a parameter used to create a new record, not a standalone URL format.

references.title: Navigate to a record or module using a URL

stem: In a ServiceNow URL, what does setting sys_id=-1 indicate?

options.text: The record does not exist and should be deleted
A new record should be created
The system should return the last modified record
The query should return all records regardless of sys_id

rationale: In ServiceNow URL parameters, setting sys_id=-1 tells the system to create a new record. Combined with sysparm_query, it applies filter values to the new record form.

distractor_notes.A: sys_id=-1 is a create signal, not a delete signal.
distractor_notes.C: There is no built-in URL parameter to retrieve the last modified record by using sys_id=-1.
distractor_notes.D: sys_id=-1 specifically means new record creation, not an all-records query.

references.title: Navigate to a record or module using a URL

stem: A developer needs a URL that returns incident records where priority is 2 AND active is true. Which sysparm_query value is correct?

options.text: sysparm_query=priority=2,active=true
sysparm_query=priority=2&active=true
sysparm_query=priority=2^active=true
sysparm_query=priority=2+active=true

rationale: In ServiceNow encoded query strings, the caret (^) separates AND conditions. The correct format is sysparm_query=priority=2^active=true.

distractor_notes.A: Commas are not valid encoded query separators in ServiceNow.
distractor_notes.B: The ampersand (&) separates URL parameters, not query conditions within sysparm_query.
distractor_notes.D: The plus sign (+) is not the ServiceNow encoded query AND operator.

references.title: Navigate to a record or module using a URL

stem: A user wants to open the Incident list view directly via URL. Which format is correct?

options.text: incident.do
incident_list.do
incident.list
list.do?table=incident

rationale: To view a list via URL, use the format table_name_list.do. For the Incident table, that is incident_list.do.

distractor_notes.A: incident.do opens a form view, not a list view.
distractor_notes.C: incident.list is the format used in the Unified Navigation filter field, not a direct URL.
distractor_notes.D: list.do?table=incident is not a valid ServiceNow URL schema.

references.title: Navigate to a record or module using a URL

stem: Which Next Experience preference category is only visible to users with the admin role?

options.text: Notifications
Accessibility
Debugging
Language and Region

rationale: The Debugging preferences appear only for users with the admin role, as they are used to detect and remove errors in Next Experience components and scripts.

distractor_notes.A: Notification preferences are available to all users.
distractor_notes.B: Accessibility preferences are available to all users.
distractor_notes.D: Language and Region preferences are available to all users.

stem: Which Next Experience preference category controls how and where a user receives system and in-product notifications, including banners and email?

options.text: Display
Accessibility
Notifications
User Experience

rationale: The Notifications preference category controls how and where users receive system and in-product notifications, including banners, badges, and delivery channels such as email.

distractor_notes.A: Display preferences control how the interface looks — layout, visual density, presentation.
distractor_notes.B: Accessibility preferences adjust the interface for accessibility needs such as keyboard navigation and contrast.
distractor_notes.D: User Experience preferences manage high-level Next Experience behaviors like enabling/disabling the experience and selecting a start page.

stem: Which Next Experience preference category lets a user set their time zone and date/time formats?

options.text: Display
User Experience
Language and Region
Workspace

rationale: The Language and Region preference category lets users define their language, time zone, and date and time formats.

distractor_notes.A: Display preferences control visual layout and density, not localization settings.
distractor_notes.B: User Experience preferences manage high-level behaviors, not time zone.
distractor_notes.D: Workspace preferences customize behavior within a specific workspace, not localization.

stem: A user searches for 'theme' in the Next Experience Preferences modal search field. What behavior does the search use?

options.text: Exact match only — the word must appear verbatim
Fuzzy search — returns results even with shortened or partial text
Regex pattern matching across all preference labels
Search is disabled in the Preferences modal

rationale: The Preferences modal search uses a fuzzy search filter, which finds applicable results even with shortened text. The Preferences panel dynamically updates as you type.

distractor_notes.A: The search is fuzzy, not exact-match only.
distractor_notes.C: Regex matching is not how the Preferences search works.
distractor_notes.D: The Preferences modal includes a search field that is fully functional.

stem: Under which condition does the Workspace preference category appear in Next Experience?

options.text: Only when the user has the admin role
Only when the user has access to Workspace and Workspace is in focus
Always, regardless of workspace access
Only on mobile devices

rationale: The Workspace preference category appears only if the user has access to Workspace and the workspace is currently in focus.

distractor_notes.A: Admin role is not the condition; workspace access and focus are.
distractor_notes.C: Workspace preferences are context-dependent, not always visible.
distractor_notes.D: Workspace preferences are not limited to mobile devices.

stem: Which keyboard shortcut favorites or unfavorites the current page in Next Experience on Windows?

options.text: Control+Alt+f
Control+Shift+f
Shift+Alt+f
Control+f

rationale: Control+Shift+f (Command+Shift+f on macOS) favorites or unfavorites the current page in Next Experience.

distractor_notes.A: Control+Alt+f is not the documented shortcut for favoriting a page.
distractor_notes.C: Shift+Alt+f is not the documented shortcut for this action.
distractor_notes.D: Control+f is a browser shortcut for find/search in the page, not a ServiceNow favorite shortcut.

stem: Which keyboard shortcut on Windows takes a user to the Next Experience instance landing page?

options.text: Control+Alt+h
Control+Alt+z
Control+Home
Control+Alt+l

rationale: Control+Alt+z (Command+Option+z on macOS) opens the instance landing page in Next Experience.

distractor_notes.A: Control+Alt+h is not the shortcut for the landing page.
distractor_notes.C: Control+Home is a browser-level shortcut to scroll to the top of the page, not a ServiceNow navigation shortcut.
distractor_notes.D: Control+Alt+l is not documented as a Next Experience keyboard shortcut.

stem: What is the Windows keyboard shortcut to impersonate a user in Next Experience?

options.text: Control+Alt+i
Control+Shift+i
Control+Alt+u
Shift+Alt+i

rationale: Control+Shift+i (Command+Shift+i on macOS) is the keyboard shortcut to impersonate a user in Next Experience.

distractor_notes.A: Control+Alt+i is not the documented impersonate shortcut.
distractor_notes.C: Control+Alt+u is not a documented Next Experience shortcut.
distractor_notes.D: Shift+Alt+i is not documented as the impersonate shortcut.

stem: In which operating system are Next Experience keyboard shortcuts currently NOT supported?

options.text: Windows
macOS
Linux
iOS

rationale: The Linux operating system is not currently supported for Next Experience keyboard shortcuts. They are documented for Windows and macOS.

distractor_notes.A: Windows is fully supported with documented keyboard shortcuts.
distractor_notes.B: macOS is fully supported with documented keyboard shortcuts using Command/Option keys.
distractor_notes.D: iOS (mobile) is a different platform; the keyboard shortcut documentation specifically calls out Linux as unsupported.

stem: From which interface can a user follow a record to receive notifications in Next Experience?

options.text: From any workspace interface
From the classic form UI only, even when Next Experience is active
From the global search results page
From the Unified Navigation notifications panel

rationale: Following records is supported from the classic form UI only, even when your instance uses Next Experience. Following records from within a workspace is not supported.

distractor_notes.A: Following records from within a workspace is explicitly not supported.
distractor_notes.C: The global search results page is for finding records, not for following them.
distractor_notes.D: The Notifications panel shows received notifications; it is not where you follow records.

references.title: Working in the Next Experience UI

stem: A developer wants a URL that opens the Incident form in the 'ess' (Employee Self-Service) view. Which parameter achieves this?

options.text: sysparm_query=view=ess
sysparm_view=ess
view=ess
sysparm_form_view=ess

rationale: The sysparm_view parameter specifies which form view to display. For example, appending sysparm_view=ess to the incident URL opens the record in the ESS view.

distractor_notes.A: sysparm_query is for record filters, not view selection.
distractor_notes.C: view=ess is not a valid standalone URL parameter in ServiceNow.
distractor_notes.D: sysparm_form_view is not a documented URL parameter; the correct parameter is sysparm_view.

references.title: Navigate to a record or module using a URL

stem: An admin wants to quickly filter an Incident list to show only records where Category equals 'Software' without opening the filter builder. What is the most direct method?

options.text: Edit the URL to add sysparm_query=category=software
Right-click the Category field value 'Software' on a record in the list and select Show Matching
Click the Category column header and select Filter
Use the global search bar to search for category:software

rationale: Quick filters allow you to filter a list by right-clicking a value in a field and selecting Show Matching. This instantly filters the list to records with that same value.

distractor_notes.A: Editing the URL works but is not the most direct method from within the list interface.
distractor_notes.C: Clicking the column header sorts the list; it does not open a filter for that value.
distractor_notes.D: Global search is for full-text searching across tables, not for applying list filters by field value.

stem: Which two components are part of the Next Experience Unified Navigation?

options.text: Global Search
Application Navigator filter field
Notifications panel
Performance Analytics dashboard

rationale: The Unified Navigation includes Global Search (to search across the instance) and Notifications (to view and personalize notifications). Both run across the top of every page.

distractor_notes.B: The Application Navigator filter field is part of the classic Core UI, not the Unified Navigation.
distractor_notes.D: Performance Analytics dashboards are reporting content within the platform, not a Unified Navigation component.

references.title: Working in the Next Experience UI

stem: Which Next Experience preference category would a user configure to change the visual density and layout of the interface?

options.text: Accessibility
Display
User Experience
Workspace

rationale: Display preferences control how the Next Experience interface looks and behaves on screen, including layout, visual density, and presentation options. These settings affect only the current user's view.

distractor_notes.A: Accessibility preferences adjust the interface for different abilities (keyboard navigation, contrast, motion), not visual density.
distractor_notes.C: User Experience preferences manage high-level behaviors like enabling/disabling Next Experience, not visual layout.
distractor_notes.D: Workspace preferences are scoped to behavior within a specific workspace.

stem: A developer needs to limit a URL-based list query to return a maximum of 5 records. Which sysparm parameter should they use?

options.text: sysparm_limit=5
sysparm_max_rows=5
sysparm_force_row_count=5
sysparm_count=5

rationale: The sysparm_force_row_count parameter limits the maximum number of results in a URL query. For example, appending sysparm_force_row_count=5 returns at most 5 records.

distractor_notes.A: sysparm_limit is used in the REST API context, not the standard platform URL parameters.
distractor_notes.B: sysparm_max_rows is not a documented URL parameter for limiting rows.
distractor_notes.D: sysparm_count is not a documented row-limiting URL parameter.

references.title: Navigate to a record or module using a URL
